SMTO-TSK-0057 — Linked-step planning was turned off for this task

GUID: 2c01e3f7-6bca-46ec-ba0b-e079bd2de900
Slug: dependency-scheduling-disabled
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • The Agent tried to plan a set of linked steps that wait for each other, but that feature was off when this task started. SMTO rejected the plan, so none of its steps ran.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Send a message asking the Agent to continue and do the steps one after another. The Agent can still do the work without linked steps, and none of the rejected steps ran.
  2. If you want the Agent to plan linked steps, open Options under the message box and turn on Dependency-aware scheduling before sending your next message. The setting is fixed when a task starts, so it only helps for new messages.

What success looks like

  • The Agent's steps start and show results in the conversation.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't change unrelated limits or time-outs to get past this; they won't affect it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Agent called schedule_activities, but the dependency-scheduling policy captured for this task has enabled=false, so graph validation rejected the whole batch.

What this means

  • The accepted dependency-scheduling policy has enabled:false when graph validation is requested. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • The accepted dependency-scheduling policy has enabled:false when graph validation is requested.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the task's captured dependency policy and supported current-run controls rather than assuming global changes update it.

How to fix it

  • The dependency_scheduling_policy is snapshotted when the task is accepted, so changing it does not affect this task. Either let the model continue with ordinary sequential tool calls, or enable Dependency-aware scheduling (composer Options, or Agent Checks for conversation/global scope) and submit a new task.
  • Execute through the supported sequential flow or enable dependency scheduling for a new task snapshot.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Work follows the accepted sequential path or a deliberately configured eligible snapshot.

What not to do

  • Do not change an unrelated timeout, budget or policy. Check whether the named setting applies only to a new task.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
